title: Evaluating medical AI systems in dermatology under uncertain ground truth
mechanism: Treats ground truth as a distribution aggregated from annotators and reports metrics with ground-truth uncertainty, instead of against one label.
adaptation: Benchmark scoring: treat each crack label as a distribution (two label versions, 2 px tolerance band) and report strict IoU, relF1@2 and a ground-truth-uncertainty interval per method.
min_experiment: No training. Recompute existing model scores with ground-truth-uncertainty intervals on CV folds and check whether the method ranking changes.
evidence: R: dermatology classification with multiple raters; shows that ground-truth uncertainty changes the evaluated accuracy (abstract not retrieved in full).

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: crack ground truth as a distribution (2021 and 2022 label versions, 2 px tolerance band); report strict IoU, relF1@2 and an interval reflecting label uncertainty, per source.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No GPU: recompute existing house and ensemble scores under both label versions and a 2 px band; report per-source intervals; adopt if ranking of methods changes for any pair within the interval.
